subject: Public FAQ wording for subprocessors & cross-border handling — hosted API/console
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: acme-legal@acme.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarification on your public subprocessor notice and transfers

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the call earlier. Before we share internally, can you send a one-paragraph plain-language summary we can publish in our procurement portal? Specifically our security team wants:

- A short explanation of what "subprocessors" means for the hosted API
- How Redwood handles cross-border transfers (SCCs, adequacy, other safeguards)
- Whether customers can opt to restrict processing to a region (console toggle or residency option)

We'd like a version we can paste into our vendor questionnaire and one slightly more detailed blurb for our legal review.

Can you also confirm whether the subprocessor list on your site is updated monthly?

Best,
Olivia
Procurement, Acme Corp

---
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on your public subprocessor notice and transfers

Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass short FAQ and a slightly expanded paragraph for legal. I copied Kimberly (privacy copy) and Laura (sales one-pager owner) to align on tone.

High-level notes in this draft:
- "Subprocessors" = third-party vendors that process customer data on Redwood's behalf (hosting, monitoring, analytics). We'll call out categories and link to the live list.
- Transfers: primary mechanism = SCCs; where an adequacy decision exists we rely on that; other safeguards include encryption in transit + contractual commitments.
- Residency: Hosted API customers can request region-restricted processing for supported models/regions; Dedicated/Private have stronger options. Add console residency toggle note.
- Subprocessor refresh cadence: default is monthly listing updates with snapshot archive (we keep historical records for at least 12 months).

Attachment: subprocessor-faq-draft.docx (contains: 1-paragraph publishable blurb; 3-paragraph legal copy; suggested UI microcopy for console).

Would appreciate Kimberly and Rishi's edits — Kimberly for plain-language tone, Rishi for legal precision. Laura — can you confirm this matches the one-pager we give prospects?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: olivia.park@acme.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on your public subprocessor notice and transfers

Thanks Markus — I ran a readability pass and attached lightweight redlines. Main suggestions:

1) Publishable blurb (one paragraph): use simpler phrasing and an explicit link to the live subprocessor list. Replace "third-party vendors" with "service providers (e.g., cloud hosting, monitoring)".

2) Residency wording: rather than "request region-restricted processing" say "select a region for processing where available" and add a short note that availability depends on model hosting support.

3) Transfers: move the SCCs sentence earlier and add a single sentence: "If you require an alternative transfer mechanism, we'll work with you during contract negotiation."

4) Add microcopy for console: label = "Data residency: Keep data in" with options and a small tooltip.

I attached redline-plainlang.txt with exact phrasing. I recommend we present both the short blurb and the legal paragraph to Acme so their questionnaire team can choose.

One small ask from sales: can we avoid the phrase "we may use subprocessors" — that's passive and scares procurement. Use active "we use the subprocessors listed here" and link.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Developer Experience — Privacy & Docs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline-plainlang.txt

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, olivia.park@acme.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 11:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on your public subprocessor notice and transfers

Looping in legal nuance — pleased with the plain-language direction. A few edits to ensure we don't inadvertently narrow contractual protections:

- Transfers: keep SCCs as the primary baseline. Add parenthetical: (Standard Contractual Clauses as adopted by the European Commission or equivalent contractual safeguards).
- Adequacy: say "where an adequacy decision applies" rather than "where an adequacy decision exists" — slightly more precise.
- Residency: we can advertise a console "Data residency" selection for hosted API, but we must include the constraint: "subject to model availability and region capacity; not all models support residency."
- Subprocessor cadence: state "public subprocessor list is updated at least monthly; customers may request a dated snapshot for audits."

Suggested 1-paragraph publishable blurb (for direct paste into procurement portals):
"Redwood uses a limited set of service providers (for infrastructure, monitoring, and analytics). Our public subprocessor list is updated at least monthly and is available here [link]. Where data is transferred across borders, we rely on appropriate legal safeguards (e.g., EU Standard Contractual Clauses) or recognized adequacy decisions. Customers can select a processing region via the Console where supported; Dedicated and Private deployments provide stronger residency guarantees. For audit evidence and historical snapshots, contact support."

If Kimberly is happy with this, I authorize: (1) publish the short blurb on our public privacy/hosted API FAQ, and (2) include the slightly expanded paragraph in the sales one-pager.

Rishi Malhotra
Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
